title: Changeset
description: Write operations (shared/operations.json) applied to one hypervideo together: all of them or none. Given to an interpreter, a changeset needs only ops (each op and input); applied, it comes back complete, with each op's inverse, so it can be shown, stored and undone. Written in the subset of JSON Schema that FrameTrailSchema implements.

id.description: Identifies the changeset, e.g. in a history. Made up when applied without one.

hypervideoId.description: The hypervideo it changes. Given, it must be the one the interpreter works on; applied, it is always set.

baseVersion.description: Given: apply only if the files are still at these versions, otherwise refuse with conflict. Applied: the versions of the files it changes before it was applied. hypervideo is meta.lastchanged of hypervideo.json; annotations is lastchanged of the user's entry in annotations/_index.json (0 while they have no annotation file). A version that is not known is left out.

createdBy.description: Id of the user who applied it: the creator of the items it adds. Set when applied.

generator.description: The software that made the changes, written as the W3C generator of every overlay and annotation the changeset adds or changes. The editor's chat panel: { "type": "Software", "name": "FrameTrail-Conversational-UI", "model": …, "provider": "mistral" }.

summary.description: What it does, in a few words: the undo step's description in the editor. The names of its operations when not given.

ops.description: The write operations, applied in this order.

input.description: Its input, as the operation's input schema describes it.

inverse.description: Set when applied: what takes the operation back, as a call of the edit interface FrameTrail's edit API and the interpreters' stores share; null when the operation changed nothing. Given, it is ignored.

method.description: add(kind, item), update(kind, ref, mergePatch), remove(kind, ref), setLayout(area, contentViews), setSubtitles(lang, vttOrNull). Kinds: overlays, annotations, chapters; refs: created, or a chapter's start.
